purpose: Counterexamples and conflicting heuristics for diagnosis and remediation. Neither law overrides accessibility, consent, security or observed user needs.

pairs.tension: Reducing available choices can simplify selection but obscure legitimate alternatives.
pairs.decision_rule: For comparable options use visible grouping/filters; narrow the *current decision*, not the available solution space.
pairs.discriminating_test: Can users find less common options and explain the recommended path?

pairs.tension: A numerical cap on items can be mistaken for meaningful grouping.
pairs.decision_rule: Cluster by domain semantics, not arbitrary 7±2 counts; externalize memory.
pairs.discriminating_test: Can users scan and recall task-relevant relationships?

pairs.tension: Familiar convention may conflict with new value enabled by a novel product.
pairs.decision_rule: Start conventional for commodity tasks; deviate only with a concrete user benefit and testing.
pairs.discriminating_test: Compare first-use success and expert efficiency across versions.

pairs.tension: A visually minimal solution can move hidden complexity onto people.
pairs.decision_rule: Remove interface elements only if user work, comprehension and error burden do not rise.
pairs.discriminating_test: Count extra calculations, clicks, memorization and recovery, not visible elements.

pairs.tension: Immediate positivity can be mistaken for durable completion in a high-stakes task.
pairs.decision_rule: Acknowledge promptly but show pending until confirmed; only show success on actual durable completion.
pairs.discriminating_test: Test delayed server response, failure and repeated submit.

pairs.tension: Large hit targets and spacing may compromise dense grouping.
pairs.decision_rule: Enlarge interaction geometry without misgrouping or overlap; use touch-responsive density and alternatives.
pairs.discriminating_test: Assess acquisition errors and grouping comprehension at multiple widths.

pairs.tension: Highly polished UI can conceal mental effort.
pairs.decision_rule: Measure actual task success, time, error and recovery in addition to perceived usability.
pairs.discriminating_test: Compare objective failures with preference ratings.

pairs.tension: Salience helps key actions but too many highlighted regions compete or resemble ads.
pairs.decision_rule: Reserve special treatment for one genuinely important state/action in context.
pairs.discriminating_test: Can users locate and correctly interpret the action under brief exposure?

pairs.tension: Flexible input handling may silently reinterpret ambiguous or high-risk user intent.
pairs.decision_rule: Normalize harmless variants; reject or seek confirmation for high-stakes ambiguity at secure boundaries.

pairs.tension: Progress can encourage completion but fake percentage or unfinished-task pressure manipulates.
pairs.decision_rule: Represent genuine work and persist unfinished tasks; respect the user’s ability to stop.
pairs.discriminating_test: Can users predict actual remaining effort and dismiss reminders?

pairs.tension: Removing tutorials might strand novices, while forced tours block their first goal.
pairs.decision_rule: Enable direct task entry with discoverable contextual help and safe practice.
pairs.discriminating_test: Measure time-to-first-value and recovery without prior instruction.

pairs.tension: Ordering by memorability or popularity can hide critical minority tasks.
pairs.decision_rule: Order by user relevance, domain convention, safety and predictable structure before primacy effects.
pairs.discriminating_test: Evaluate findability across infrequent but critical tasks.

pairs.tension: Uniform components may appear grouped even when semantic parentage differs.
pairs.decision_rule: Use visual grouping plus real DOM heading, label, landmark and component semantics.
pairs.discriminating_test: Does visible grouping match assistive-tech relationships?
